Guided tours have stopped completely and been replaced by audio guides.

stem.en:
The decision to close the Harlan footbridge to cyclists was not taken lightly. Although cyclists had used it for decades without serious accident, engineers from the council found that the vibration of heavy electric bikes was loosening the bolts on the oldest section. Cyclists must now use the road bridge, which adds a few minutes to their journey. The footbridge will reopen to them once the old section has been strengthened.

Which sentence means the same as the second sentence of the text?

options.en: Though cyclists had crossed safely for decades, engineers found heavy e-bikes shaking loose the bolts of the oldest section.
Engineers closed the bridge because cyclists had caused a number of serious accidents on it.
The bolts on the oldest section had slowly worked loose over many decades of use, so heavy bikes were banned from it.
Engineers found that heavy electric bikes had damaged the road bridge, not the footbridge.

why.en: "Although ... for decades without serious accident" = "Though cyclists had crossed safely for decades"; e-bikes shake the bolts loose. There were no accidents, and age alone is not the cause.

The fields were productive at first, but the peat soil slowly shrank as it dried, and the land sank below the level of the river. This is why the farmers themselves, rather than any outside group, have asked for the pumps to be switched off and the marsh allowed to return.

The crops are now worth more each year than it costs to pump the fields.
Pumping has made the fields grow more valuable crops every year.
The cost of pumping is rising, but the crops are still worth more.

The line is run mainly as a museum piece for tourists who visit it at weekends.

stem.en:

The critics were right: every kind of shop has lost customers.

Some members say that progress is faster, because each leader brings new ideas.

The choir makes slow progress because its leaders all have the same habits.

stem.en:

But fish numbers only began to rise after a second, less noticed change: farmers along the banks agreed to leave a strip of wild grass between their fields and the river, which catches the soil and fertiliser washed off by rain. options.en: Probably both the treatment works and the grass strips were needed.
The treatment works alone explain why the fish came back.
The grass strips along the banks had a much greater effect on the river than the treatment works did.
Fish numbers rose as soon as the treatment works opened.

why.en: "Most likely, it took both changes together": the works cut waste, but fish rose "only ... after" the grass strips. Neither change is said to matter more than the other.

The meadows that seem to have grown by chance are in fact cut at carefully chosen times, so that early flowers can drop their seed before the grass is mown and later ones can grow undisturbed. The meadows are never cut, so that both early and late flowers can drop their seed.
The meadows are cut at random times through the year, which is exactly why they look as if they grew by chance.
The early flowers are cut before they seed, so that the later ones have more room.
